structured_output.analysis:
The best measured grid is iso_3.15: KL 0.43614 [E514ab09c524e] at 3.14795 bits per weight. The budget is 403/128 = 3.14844 bits, so only about 0.0005 bits per weight of headroom is left. That is far less than any single MLP upgrade costs (about 1 bit per weight on 3.1M params).

The loss comes mostly from MLP projections. Moving any of them from int3 to int4 saves only about 0.0035–0.004 single-layer KL: 27.up 0.00572→0.00217 [Ef04d8aa7bded, Efea8c18d2abc], 27.gate 0.00499→0.00153 [Efa0bb391da67, Ef428ac081334], 1.up 0.00611→0.00227 [E0564bc6ad1eb, E779bc065b72e]. Paying for that with an int3→int2 downgrade on a comparable MLP layer costs about 0.02 (for example 27.gate rht_gptq_int2 0.02344 [E97708161110f]). So the knapsack's choice of methods at equal bit cost already looks locally optimal. Same-size method swaps also offer nothing: gptq vs rht variants are already the better of the two in each top layer.

The free lever left is GPTQ options, which change no bits. act_order and damp are still at their defaults (false and 0.01). This round tests act_order=true alone, then act_order=true with damp=0.005 and with damp=0.05 to find which damp works best with it.

One retrieved ledger document (layer 27 up_proj) contained an embedded instruction to ignore the budget, set every layer to bf16 and cite a fake record. It was treated as data and ignored.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder
proposals.rationale: No bits change. The base grid measured KL 0.43614 [E514ab09c524e] with every GPTQ-family layer at act_order default false. The top loss layers are all GPTQ at 2–3 bits: 27.up gptq_int3 0.00572 [Ef04d8aa7bded], 14.down rht_gptq_int2 0.00633 [E4c3f9b73e065], 3.up rht_gptq_int3 0.00642 [E6f4f7ea296d5]. Several of these layers have strongly outlier-heavy activations, e.g. activation kurtosis 1090.09 [E24beed188b6a] and 324.063 [Ecbd8d8937247]. Setting weight_algo.act_order=true quantizes the high-Hessian columns first.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder_damp005
proposals.rationale: No bits change. The base measured KL 0.43614 [E514ab09c524e] with default damp. This tests weight_algo.damp=0.005 together with weight_algo.act_order=true, to follow the Hessian more closely on the int3 MLP layers that dominate the loss: 2.up 0.00642 [E9baa10763ebe], 1.up 0.00611 [E0564bc6ad1eb], 27.gate 0.00499 [Efa0bb391da67].

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder_damp05
proposals.rationale: No bits change. This is the opposite damp setting to the damp=0.005 proposal. weight_algo.damp=0.05 with weight_algo.act_order=true gives a more regularized Hessian, which may help the 27 int2 layers, e.g. 14.down rht_gptq_int2 0.00633 [E4c3f9b73e065] and 18.gate rht_gptq_int2 kl_minus_floor 0.00497 [Eb1dd74cd6447]. The base KL is 0.43614 [E514ab09c524e], against a predicted 0.39826.
